text:
maria_ml: Heads up — running into messy OTEL behavior across our inference services. Python app and Go router both register global TracerProviders in different places and spans are duplicated when we sidecar the exporter.
kevin_platform: ugh. do you have an example? sounds like init ordering + double-init issue.
sophie_infra: include envs please. OTEL_ variables can mask bugs.
maria_ml: repro: Python service sets tracer with our lib on import; router (Go) uses SDK auto-instrumentation and sets another provider in main. When requests cross process boundary, we see duplicate root spans and weird resource attrs.
raj_sre: could be differing resource attributes merging. do we set service.name consistently? Also check Propagators.
maria_ml: we use `service.name=redwood-inference` in python, `redwood-router` in go. Propagators: python uses `tracecontext,baggage`, go was default (maybe not). devbot: [deploy-bot] canary rolled back: tracer-provider-fix -> failed healthchecks :warning:
kevin_platform: two actionables: 1) document recommended init pattern (lazy init via SDK init func, not on import). 2) add small guard in our libs that no-ops if a provider already registered and config.force=false.
sophie_infra: +1. Also propose we surface an env `REDWOOD_OTEL_INIT=auto|none|explicit` and default `auto` that respects existing provider.
maria_ml: second issue: KV cache hits/ misses need explicit spans. Right now we emit a `kv.cache` span only on miss. That skews latency histograms.
raj_sre: yep, we need bool attribute `cache.hit=true/false` on the request span, and a child span for heavy misses which includes `kv.store.time_ms` and `fetch.source`.
kevin_platform: also consider linking spans instead of nested child when we resume execution after KV async fetch. avoids confusing timeline in traces.
sophie_infra: exporter behavior: Go exporter batches aggressively and flushes on shutdown; Python exporter default batch size is tiny. We should align OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_BATCH_SIZE and timeouts across languages.
maria_ml: proposed export defaults: batch_size=512, timeout_ms=2000, max_queue=2048. Env overrides allowed via `REDWOOD_OTEL_BATCH_*`.
raj_sre: retention note: platform retention TTL is 30d for production. But we want sampling at edge to drop noisy inference-internal traces. Suggest deterministic sampling by model.hash for lower-SKU models.
kevin_platform: sampling decision needs to run before expensive spans created. So sampler must be invoked in middleware before any KV or model spans. We'll add a sampler hook upstream.
kevin_platform: pseudocode idea:
```
// in request middleware
sample = sampler.should_sample(ctx, {model_id, route, user_tier})
if !sample { set_trace_sampler(AlwaysOff) }
// continue
```
maria_ml: tests: add unit test that env `REDWOOD_OTEL_INIT=explicit` prevents auto register and that duplicate provider not created. Also integration test to assert `cache.hit` attr present in root span.
sophie_infra: telemetry dashboard mapping: map `model.version`, `route.policy`, `cache.hit`, `tokens.requested`, `tokens.generated` as top-level columns. We should add clear naming conventions: `redwood.model.version` etc.
raj_sre: alerting: firing if `kv.store.time_ms` P99 > 200ms per route for 5m.
kevin_platform: small perf note: Rust inference bridge (FFI) needs nonblocking OTEL calls — ensure OTEL exporters aren't doing sync network IO on hot path. Use async buffers + backpressure.
maria_ml: next step: I'll open 3 PRs — python lib guard + env, go router sampler hook + exporter config, and infra doc for dashboard columns + retention. Assigning to @kevin_platform and @sophie_infra for reviews.
kevin_platform: will review go PR today.
sophie_infra: will add dashboard skeleton and retention runbook.
devbot: [ci-bot] lint passed for branch otel-kvcache-sampling, tests 128/130 — flaky model tests failing. :slightly_smiling_face:
maria_ml: thanks all. tagging follow-ups in the PRs. we should also sync with product before sampling defaults change in prod.
